headline: Natural laws are patterns that never break—the universe's consistent rules that enable prediction
universal_truth: Some rules are universal; finding them enables prediction and power; nature is lawful, not random
fun_facts: Gravity works the same everywhere in the universe—no exceptions have ever been found
Conservation of energy is so reliable that apparent violations have always led to new discoveries
Newton's laws were used to predict Neptune's existence before it was ever observed
discussion_questions: What 'laws' have you discovered in your own domain—patterns that never seem to break?
How do you distinguish between rules and guidelines in your life?
What would you do differently if you knew certain rules were absolute?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Drop anything, anywhere, anytime—it falls. Energy is never created or destroyed—it just moves. Some rules never break. These are natural laws: the universe's consistent patterns. Finding them gives us power to predict and control.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We have guidelines that sometimes work and laws that always work. What's the difference and why does it matter?

options.text: Laws are universal and exceptionless—they've never been observed to break; this reliability enables prediction; you can count on laws in ways you can't count on guidelines
options.response: Yes. Laws are rules without exceptions—so reliable that planning around them is safe. This reliability is what makes science predictive and technology possible.

options.text: Laws are just very strong patterns
options.response: They're patterns, but their exceptionless nature is what makes them laws—we've never seen them break...

q1.title: Universal Reliability
q1.script: Natural laws work everywhere, every time. Gravity doesn't take days off. Energy is always conserved. This universality is what makes them laws, not just patterns.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Universal Reliability"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Prediction Power
q2.script: Laws enable prediction. If something always happens, you can count on it happening. This reliability underlies all technology—we build machines trusting that laws hold.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Finding Your Laws
q3.script: Are there 'laws' in your domain? Patterns that never break? Relationships that always hold? Finding your version of natural laws gives you predictive power in your world.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Some rules are universal. Finding them enables prediction and power. Nature is lawful, not random. Discover the laws that govern your domain.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 300! A major milestone—300 days of learning! Tomorrow, we'll explore how likely things are. Until then, appreciate the reliable rules that make prediction possible.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.
